info.title: Aithos Agent Card Registry
info.summary: A public registry of signed A2A Agent Cards, where the key is the account.
info.description:
Anyone may publish an Agent Card; the card is signed by its owner's key; only
a holder of an authorized key can change it. There are no accounts, no
passwords and no sessions, so no endpoint here takes a credential — a write
is authorized by a signature over the operation, carried in the request body.

An entry may also certify ownership of domains, each proved by a record in
that domain's own DNS zone.

Two documents are normative and this one is not:

- [`SPEC.md`](https://github.com/aithos-protocol/registry/blob/main/SPEC.md)
  — identity model, card processing, writes, public endpoints, limits, and
  the problem table.
- [`DOMAIN-CERTIFICATION.md`](https://github.com/aithos-protocol/registry/blob/main/DOMAIN-CERTIFICATION.md)
  — the domain certification profile, additive to the above.

---

SPEC.md is normative and this document is not. Where the two disagree, SPEC.md wins and this document is the defect.

It is written by hand rather than derived from the code, for the same reason the field-presence table of SPEC.md §5.2 is: a description generated from an implementation documents that implementation, including its mistakes, and stops being a second opinion about what the protocol says. The cost of writing it by hand is drift, so drift is what the test guards — `crates/registry-api/tests/openapi.rs` fails when the operations here stop matching the router, or when the problem codes stop matching the catalogue, SPEC.md §9 or the published problem pages.

JSON rather than YAML because this file is served verbatim at `/v1/openapi.json`: there is no build step between what is reviewed here and what a client fetches, and the test reads it with the JSON parser the service already depends on.

servers.description: Development. Writes here are real and equally permanent.

tags.name: read
tags.description:
Anonymous and read-only. Served from the object store behind the CDN, never
from compute — which is why a withdrawn entry answers `404` here and the
record (§7.3) is where its status is stated.

tags.name: write
tags.description:
Rare, and authorized by a signature over the operation rather than by a
credential. Each carries its own signed payload; none accepts an
`Authorization` header, because there is nothing to put in one.

tags.name: discovery
tags.description: What this registry pins, accepts and limits.

get.summary: What this registry pins, accepts and limits
get.description:
The canonical origin, the pinned A2A commit, accepted `alg` values, the
limits of §8, the domain certification parameters, and a digest of the
field-presence table of §5.2.

The presence-table digest is the load-bearing member. A2A pins a protocol
commit but publishes no table derived from it, so two implementations can
read the same commit and still disagree about one field — which yields two
canonical documents and two signatures over what looks like the same card.
The digest turns "we pinned the same commit" into something a second
implementation can check.

Cursor-paginated. There is no search, no ranking and no scoring, and
entries carry no badge of any kind.

Ties on `updatedAt` are broken by `agentId`, so the order is total and a
cursor can neither skip nor repeat an entry. **A client ends a listing on
an empty page, not on a missing `nextCursor`**: the registry may return a
cursor whenever the page filled, without knowing whether anything follows.

200.description: One page of entries. Records in a listing carry no `domains` member — an absent member says "not stated here", where an empty one would claim there are none.

get.summary: The registration record for an entry
get.description:
A projection: status, current digest, the authorized key set, timestamps,
certified domains and same-origin links. It is a convenience, never a
substitute for verifying the card.

This is also the only endpoint that distinguishes a withdrawn entry from
one that never existed: it answers `200` with `status: WITHDRAWN`, where
the card and key-set paths answer `404` for both.

put.summary: Publish a card, creating or updating the entry
put.description:
`agentId` is client-derived — the RFC 7638 thumbprint of the genesis key —
so the address is known before anything is published and this operation
needs no server-allocated identifier.

The body carries the card, the public keys that signed it, and **one
publication proof per key entering the authorized set**: the set of proof
signers must equal the set of card signers. A key that signed the card but
produced no proof is `UNPROVEN_KEY`.

That requirement is not bookkeeping. A card's signing payload is public the
moment the card is published, so anyone can append a signature to someone
else's card without invalidating the original; were one proof enough, an
attacker could open an entry in their own name whose published key set
names a holder who never asked for it.

**Idempotent by construction.** Submitting bytes identical to the current
version answers `200` and changes nothing, including the sequence — which
is exactly what a client retrying after a network timeout does, and its
earlier write may well have succeeded. Different bytes at the same version
are still refused by §6.4.

200.description: The entry was updated, or the submitted bytes were already the current version.

delete.description:
In V1 because the registry never holds the publisher's key: the publisher
must be able to remove their own entry without asking an operator.

The signed payload names the current `cardDigest`, which is what prevents
an older withdrawal being replayed.

The entry becomes `WITHDRAWN`, and the registry stops serving its current
card and its JWKS. Published versions remain readable at their digest —
what was published is not erased, only its status changes. The `agentId`
is never reusable.

200.description: The entry is withdrawn. The record it returns lists no domains.

get.summary: The current card, as the exact bytes that were signed
get.description:
The body is `cardBytes` verbatim. The registry never re-serializes a stored
card on read, because a re-serialized card is a different document and its
signatures no longer verify.

**`ETag` is opaque**, in the sense of RFC 9110, and a client must not parse
it as a digest. The API origin happens to derive it from the card digest;
the CDN origin serves whatever validator the object store computed — two
origins, two shapes, one endpoint. A client that needs the digest computes
it from the bytes it received, which is not a workaround but the only
correct behaviour: a digest handed over by the same server whose answer it
is meant to check establishes nothing.

**On `404` and `410`.** The API origin distinguishes a withdrawn entry from
an absent one; the CDN origin, which serves objects the reconciler deletes
on withdrawal, has nothing left to answer `410` from. Consumers MUST treat
`404` from this path as "no current card" without inferring which of the
two it means, and read the record (§7.3) when the difference matters.

304.description: Not modified. The comparison is weak, as RFC 9110 §13.1.2 requires for `If-None-Match`.

get.description:
Each key carries its `kid` — the RFC 7638 thumbprint of that key, matching
the `kid` in the `protected` header of any signature it produced.

The registry rebuilds each entry from the key material it verified rather
than republishing the JWK as submitted, so a submitter cannot place a
`kid`, an `alg` or any other member of their choosing into the published
set. The only members served are `kty`, `crv`, the coordinates, `kid` and
`use: "sig"`.

A withdrawn entry serves nothing here, with the same `404` shape as the
card path.

get.summary: The publication history of an entry

200.description: One page of versions, each addressable at its digest.

get.summary: One historical version, by its digest
get.description:
Immutable exact bytes. The digest is in the request path, so it never needs
carrying in a header, and these responses are cached for a year.

One version has one URL. `{cardDigest}` must be the exact form the registry
publishes — `sha256:` then 64 lowercase hex characters — and any other
spelling, the bare hex included, is `404`: a second spelling would be a
second permanently cached entry for the same bytes, with its own `ETag`.

200.description: The card bytes of that version.

put.summary: Certify the domains an entry owns
put.description:
Two assertions, each made where that side actually has authority: the
domain speaks in its own DNS zone, and the key speaks by signing. Neither
half alone is accepted — a zone has no authority over someone's key, and a
signed request naming `example.com` establishes nothing about
`example.com`.

The signed `domains` array is the **complete set**: it replaces whatever
was there, and an empty array removes every certification. There is no
separate deletion operation, for the same reason there is no rotation
operation — the request states the whole set, and stating a smaller one is
how you shrink it.

The payload carries no `cardDigest`, unlike a withdrawal: a certification
is a statement about domains, not about a card, and binding it to a digest
would expire every certification at the next publish for no gain.

Only what the registry can currently observe is published. It re-resolves
every requested domain hourly; a domain missing for three consecutive
passes stops being listed and returns by itself when its record does.

200.description: The record, with `domains` showing what the registry observed.

422.description:
The request was refused. When a domain's record could not be observed,
the problem carries a `domains` member reporting the outcome for each
one, so a publisher learns every missing record at once rather than one
per attempt.

AgentId.name: agentId
AgentId.description: The RFC 7638 thumbprint of the genesis key — 43 base64url characters, computable offline before anything is published.

CardDigest.name: cardDigest
CardDigest.description: Exactly as the registry publishes it. Any other spelling is `404`.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size. Values outside the range are clamped, not refused.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description:
Opaque, and belonging to the registry that issued it. One this registry did
not issue — or one naming an entry it no longer holds — is
`400 CURSOR_INVALID`, never silently the first page.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description:
The digest of the version this write expects to replace. Comparison is
strong, the opposite of the weak comparison `If-None-Match` uses on reads,
because this one guards a write.

ETag.description: An opaque validator in the sense of RFC 9110. Clients MUST NOT parse it as a digest.

AgentId.description: An RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint, base64url, unpadded.

Digest.description: `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex characters. The bare hex is not this.

Domain.description: An A-label, lowercase. Not a public suffix.

Jwk.description:
A public JWK. Private members are refused outright with
`PRIVATE_KEY_SUBMITTED` — the registry has no use for one, and a key
holder who sent one by accident needs to hear so rather than have it
quietly accepted.

Jws.description:
A detached JWS in flattened form (RFC 7515). `protected.kid` MUST be the
RFC 7638 thumbprint of the key that verifies it — that single rule carries
the whole authorization design, because the thumbprint is a digest of the
key material, so a public key submitted in a plain request body cannot be
swapped for another.

payload.description: `BASE64URL(UTF8(JCS(payload)))`, verbatim — so a signature can never cover bytes that differ from what the registry reads.

SignedAgentCard.description:
A complete A2A AgentCard including its `signatures[]`, pinned to A2A v1.0.1
at commit `3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991`. Parsing is strict:
RFC 8785 canonicalization, I-JSON, no duplicate members, and the
field-presence rules of SPEC.md §5.2 — whose derivation digest is in the
manifest.

name.description: Self-declared. Nobody checked it, and an interface MUST show the thumbprint rather than this as the identity of an entry.

version.description: The card's own semver version. A publication must move it strictly forward.

keys.description: The public keys that signed the card. Every proof signer must be among them, and no key may appear twice.

proofs.description:
One per key entering the authorized set, each a JWS over a
`PublishPayload`. On a creation, one proof's `kid` must equal the
`agentId` — the genesis key names the entry, so the genesis key is what
asks for the entry to exist. On an update, at least one proof must come
from the current authorized set.

PublishPayload.description:
The decoded `payload` of a publication proof, exactly. Extra members are
refused. `registryOrigin` binds the proof to one registry, so a card and
its proof cannot be lifted from one and replayed into another.

WithdrawPayload.description: The decoded `payload` of a withdrawal, exactly. `cardDigest` must equal the current version's digest, which is what prevents replay of an older withdrawal.

CertifyPayload.description:
The decoded `payload` of a certification, exactly. Extra members are
refused, and `cardDigest` is deliberately absent.

domains.description:
Sorted in ascending code-point order, with no duplicate. JCS orders
object members but not array elements, so array order is signed as
submitted; requiring one order makes the payload a deterministic
function of the set. An unsorted or duplicated array is
`DOMAINS_NOT_CANONICAL`. An empty array removes every certification.

certifiedAt.description: First observation in the current continuous run.

AgentRecord.description:
A projection of registration facts, and nothing about whether the thing at
this address is honest. The card's self-declared `name` and endpoints are
not repeated here.

cardVersion.description: The A2A card's own version field.

authorizedKids.description: The current authorized set — the keys that signed the current version. Rotation is the choice of which keys sign; there is no rotation operation.

domains.description:
What the registry can currently observe, sorted — never what was once
requested. **Absent rather than empty** where the registry is not
stating it, as in a listing: an absent member says "not stated here",
where an empty one would claim there are none.

nextCursor.description: May be present on a full page even when nothing follows. End on an empty page, not on its absence.

documentation.description: Where this surface is described, and where the `type` URI of every problem document resolves. Both are static objects on this origin: a client that found the registry can reach its documentation without being told a second hostname.

claim.description: What an entry in this registry states, in one sentence — and what it does not.

presenceTable.description: A digest of the field-presence table of §5.2, and what it was derived from.

Problem.description:
RFC 9457. Every refusal the registry makes is one, including refusals made
before a handler runs — a body stopped by the size limit, a malformed query
parameter, an unroutable path.

Two refusals carry no `code` and must be handled by status alone: a `429`
from the gateway's own throughput limit, and a `403` from the edge for a
method a cached read path does not serve. A rate block carries every member
of a problem document but the media type `application/json`, because the
edge firewall's body types do not include `application/problem+json`.

type.description: Dereferences to human-readable documentation for the code: `/problems/{code}`, lowercased with `-` for `_`.

pointer.description: An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the offending member, so a client can highlight it rather than being told the card is invalid.

domains.description: The outcome per domain, so a publisher learns every missing record at once.

PublicationProof.description: A JWS whose payload asks this registry to publish this card under this identifier.

Withdrawal.description: A JWS whose payload asks this registry to withdraw this entry.

Certification.description: A JWS whose payload states the complete set of domains to certify.

NotAuthorized.description: `NOT_AUTHORIZED_KEY` — no signature by a currently authorized key.

NotFound.description: `NOT_FOUND`. On the card and key-set paths this may also mean withdrawn; the record says which.

Withdrawn.description: `WITHDRAWN` — the entry was withdrawn by its key holder, and the identifier is never reusable.

WriteConflict.description: `AGENT_ID_MISMATCH`, `VERSION_NOT_INCREASING`, `CERTIFICATION_NOT_INCREASING`, or `CONFLICT` — a concurrent write changed the entry first.

PreconditionFailed.description: `PRECONDITION_FAILED` — `If-Match` did not match the current digest.

TooLarge.description: `CARD_TOO_LARGE`. Checked before the body is parsed, and so before any signature is verified.

Unprocessable.description: The request was well formed and refused on its content — a signature, a key, or the card itself.

CursorInvalid.description: `CURSOR_INVALID` — the cursor did not come from this registry. Never silently the first page.

RateLimited.description:
`RATE_LIMITED`, per source address and per `agentId`. Carries every member
of a problem document, but with media type `application/json`: the edge
firewall refuses a header overriding the content type. A client keying on
`code` reads it; one keying on the media type alone does not.
